subject: history

moments.title: Beveridge Report
moments.body: December 1942: 'Social Insurance and Allied Services' identifies five 'giant evils' — want, disease, ignorance, squalor, idleness. Beveridge proposes universal social insurance and a national health service. The report sells 600,000 copies — extraordinary for a government document.
moments.takeaway: Beveridge framed postwar reconstruction. The 1945 Labour landslide built on the consensus the report had begun.

moments.title: Labour landslide
moments.body: 5 July 1945: Labour wins 393 seats to the Conservatives' 197. Attlee becomes Prime Minister. The mandate: implement Beveridge. Family Allowances Act (1945), National Insurance Act (1946), National Health Service Act (1946).
moments.takeaway: The 1945-51 Labour government nationalised coal, rail, road haulage, gas, electricity, the Bank of England, and steel. The welfare state and the mixed economy were created together.

moments.title: NHS launched
moments.body: 5 July 1948: the NHS opens. Free at the point of use, funded by taxation, available to all. Bevan had to break the BMA's resistance — 'I stuffed their mouths with gold,' he later said of consultant contracts that retained private practice rights.

quote.text: No society can legitimately call itself civilised if a sick person is denied medical aid because of lack of means.
quote.attrib: Aneurin Bevan, In Place of Fear, 1952

moments.takeaway: The NHS treated 30 million within its first year. Demand was vastly higher than predicted — the suppressed health needs of the working class were enormous.

now.title: Britain's most cherished institution
now.body: The NHS remains universally free at point of use, though prescription charges (England), dental and optical fees apply. The 2012 London Olympics opening ceremony featured the NHS centrally. Funding squeezes since 2010, COVID-19, and waiting list growth have intensified debate. 1.5 million staff make it the largest UK employer.
now.open_questions: Is the model sustainable? Reform proposals — co-payments, social insurance — recur in policy debate. Public attachment to free-at-point-of-use principles has been remarkably durable.

reflection: Postwar Britain made the conscious decision that health care should not depend on income. 75 years later, despite continual stress, the principle has held. The NHS is the rare political institution that defines a national self-image.
